patch_description: The theoretical optimum for n=14 in 3D is a well-studied Tammes/packing-type problem; the soft-min annealing converges to ≈0.24 squared ratio but the unconstrained L-BFGS-B polish on the exact ratio is weak because dmin is non-smooth (only one active pair at a time). Following the recommendation, I add a constrained SLSQP polish that maximizes t subject to d²ᵢⱼ ≤ 1 (fixing scale) and d²ᵢⱼ ≥ t², applied to the top-3 candidates after annealing with symmetry-breaking perturbations. The constraint Jacobian is filled per-pair in a plain loop (the vectorized fancy-index version crashed in Gen 21 due to a shape mismatch). Since the constraint set keeps dmax ≤ 1 and pushes dmin up, this directly maximizes the true metric. To save time, the SLSQP polish replaces the per-seed L-BFGS-B exact-ratio polish for all but the ranking stage: we rank seeds by soft-annealed ratio, keep top 3, then SLSQP each (plus perturbed restarts). Eval budget stays small (~2-3s).
